Subject: Anchored onramp + burst structure for Dedicated capacity — HelioMed Systems

Amanda / team —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our call I pulled together three differentiated Dedicated offers that balance predictable baseline capacity with the burstability HelioMed needs for weekend inference spikes and quarterly model retrains. I attached a one‑page options summary (HelioMed_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf) and the usage estimate we ran against your logs (heliomed_usage_estimate_aug.csv).

High level (details in attachment):
- Option A — Anchored slab (recommended): 24 gpus reserved (min floor 8 GPUs), ramp to 24 over 90 days. Includes 10% prewarm credits and a weekend burst pool up to +40% for 12 hours/day. SLA: 99.9% availability on floor, 95th pct latency commitment for standard gen routes.
- Option B — Staggered ladder: start 12 gpus (min floor 6), staged increases month 1 -> 12, month 2 -> 18, month 3 -> 24. Lower monthly commit first three months; smaller overage rate for burst.
- Option C — Flexible core + burst: 8 gpus core (min floor 4) + reserved burst pool (pay-for-burst hours) that you can trigger for scheduled retrains / spikes. Best if you prefer capital flexibility but we lose some steady‑latency guarantees.

Key tradeoffs we discussed: unit cost vs. latency SLO, prewarm credits / warm cache behavior, and fallback model variants (quantized cheaper variant triggered automatically if burst capacity exhausted). In the attachment I included 24/16/8 GPU profiles with expected p95 latency, estimated monthly token burn, and a 12‑month pricing curve.

Next steps: can you confirm which option you want to examine in a redline for contract terms? If helpful we can also run a 2‑week pilot on Option A with a soft‑commit credit to show steady p95 under your workload.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0182
Redwood Inference — Dedicated & Private deployments

Amanda / procurement —

Thanks for the questions. Below is a concise month‑by‑month mapping and clarifications on the burst and prewarm behavior. I'm including internal ops notes for Karthik / Priyom to confirm runtime behavior and any activation lead times.

Month mapping (Option A — anchored slab / recommended):
- Start (day 0): Contract effective; onboarding sprint begins. Activation: allocate 8 GPUs (active), 16 GPUs parked (warm) so your min billing floor = 8 GPUs.
- Month 1: Billing floor increases to 12 GPUs (soft ramp), expected effective capacity 16 GPUs during business hours; weekend burst up to +30% (parked warm nodes kept ready).
- Month 2: Billing floor = 18 GPUs; weekend burst +40% available; prewarm cache coverage expands to commonly hit prefixes.
- Month 3: Billing floor = 24 GPUs (steady state).

Minimum / billing: the "min floor" is contractual for baseline reserved capacity you pay for. For Option A we bill the floor (8/12/18/24 per months as above) and provide a discounted overage rate for burst hours beyond the reserved slab. Overage is hourly and only charged when burst triggers run.

Burst mechanics: for Option A we recommend a hybrid approach — we prepark (warm) a subset of nodes so spin‑up is near‑instant (< 2 mins for most routes). For larger scheduled retrains you can prebook additional reserved burst hours at a lower rate (we show both on attachment). If spare fleet capacity is used, fallback is via quantized model variant with a soft latency increase (configurable threshold).

Prewarm credits: Pilot: we offer up to 1200 prewarm credits (equivalent to ~48 GPU‑hours of prewarmed cache availability) at no charge for a single 2‑week pilot. Post pilot, prewarm is billed as part of the commit (Option A includes 10% prewarm credit built into month pricing). Credits are applied before overage calculations.

Operational notes for engineering (internal):
- Karthik: confirm <2 min spin‑up for 1k concurrent inference sessions on the preparked nodes and any kernel precompilation required.
- Priyom: flag any model quantization fallback variants we should automatically enable once burst overage crosses 80% of reserved slab.

Commercials (summary):
- Option A (24 GPU target): Monthly commit (steady) $XX,XXX after ramp; pilot discount for months 1–2; overage hourly at $YY/hr per GPU; prewarm credits included = 10%.
- Option B (staggered): lower month‑1 commit, incremental increases; slightly higher per‑GPU rate during month‑1.
- Option C (core + pay‑for‑burst): lower baseline, higher variable cost for heavy retrains.

I attached an updated row‑level pricing tab in HelioMed_Dedicated_Options_v3.pdf with the month mapping and a sample invoice view. If this looks good I'll generate a formal SOW/term sheet for procurement and a DocuSign link.

Vanessa Ortiz
